subsystems.name: Vehicle battery and power electronics
subsystems.role: stores energy and manages bidirectional power flow.

subsystems.name: Bidirectional charger
subsystems.role: converts between grid AC and vehicle DC in both directions.

subsystems.name: Communication and control
subsystems.role: coordinates charging and discharging with grid signals.

subsystems.name: Aggregation platform
subsystems.role: pools many vehicles to act as a single grid resource.

subsystems.name: Grid interface and protection
subsystems.role: connects the charger to the distribution network safely.

buildSteps.title: Make vehicles V2G-capable
buildSteps.detail: Ensure the battery and power electronics can handle bidirectional power, and unlock software where hardware already supports it.

buildSteps.title: Deploy bidirectional chargers
buildSteps.detail: Install AC or DC chargers that can invert power, at homes, depots or public sites.

buildSteps.title: Implement communication standards
buildSteps.detail: Adopt protocols such as ISO 15118-20 for bidirectional power transfer and OCPP for charger management.

buildSteps.title: Build aggregation software
buildSteps.detail: Develop a platform to manage many vehicles, forecast availability, and bid into grid markets.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with the grid operator
buildSteps.detail: Agree on interconnection, protection settings and market rules for discharging to the grid.

buildSteps.title: Run pilot fleets
buildSteps.detail: Test with a small group of vehicles to validate performance, battery wear and grid impact.

buildSteps.title: Scale up
buildSteps.detail: Expand to more vehicles, sites and markets as regulations and standards mature.

prerequisites.why: some vehicles and chargers support it, but it is not standard equipment.
ISO 15118-20 and related standards exist, but adoption is limited.
some regions allow V2G, many do not yet have rules for it.
pilots demonstrate the concept, but mature commercial platforms are few.
millions of EVs are on the road, providing a large potential resource.

pathway.milestone: pilot projects demonstrate V2G for frequency regulation and peak shaving
pathway.unlocks: proof that vehicles can provide grid services without undue battery wear.

pathway.milestone: commercial V2G for fleets with predictable schedules
pathway.unlocks: a revenue stream for depot operators and a flexible grid resource.

pathway.milestone: residential V2G in markets with supportive regulation
pathway.unlocks: households can earn from their cars while parked.

pathway.milestone: V2G integrated into grid planning as a standard resource
pathway.unlocks: millions of vehicles stabilising the grid and enabling more renewables.
